findings: Anchors: extraction + live-page (keviniscooking.com fetched cleanly; page matches the transcription line for line, including grape tomatoes and the 7-step method). All three battery fails on the re-run are tool artifacts against the repaired spec, verified by hand: (1) scale-ratio/feta - battery reads only '1 lb' from the compound buy string '1 lb 6 oz feta cheese, crumbled (635 g)'; 635 g is 2.80x of the source 8 oz, consistent with the recipe's 2.75x plus quantization (spinach and artichokes sit at 2.8x the same way). (2) prose-numbers - battery's regex reads '51.8 grams of protein' as '8g' and '16.1 grams of carbs' as '1g'; the prose figures 561/51.8/16.1 are the spec's own locked macros, which round to the stat's 561/52/16; writer_notes declare them verbatim. (3) coverage - 'Cherry Tomatoes' vs 'grape tomatoes' is a commodity-canon stand-in only (display and buy strings say grape tomatoes, 5 1/2 cups = 2 cups x 2.75); 'Garlic' vs 'garlic cloves' is the same food (8 cloves = 3 x 2.75 rounded). Both substitutions deliberate and defensible. NOTE findings, non-blocking: (a) olives interpreted as drained weight per 14.5 oz can (728 g across three cans, ~9.3 oz drained per source can) - reasonable reading of '14.5 oz black olives (drained)'; (b) lemons rounded 5.5 -> 6 for purchasability; (c) salt written as table salt vs source kosher salt, flagged intentionally in writer_notes. Method, title, credit and servings all faithful. TOOLING NOTE for the battery owner: coverage_check.py cannot parse compound weights ('1 lb 6 oz') or decimal prose figures ('51.8 grams'), which produced all three false fails here and will recur on other recipes.
